title: Proof of Concept study for determination of calcium and magnesium levels in blood serum and cerebrospinal fluid after intravenous application of magnesium sulfate in patients with aneurysmatic subarachnoid hemorrhage
summary:
Background:
Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening disease of the central nervous system and commonly caused by a rupture of the wall of a pathologically enlarged vessle (aneurysm). Despite best medical treatment, about 1/3 of the patients pass away due to the initial bleeding or its´ related complications. In particular, the occurrence of cerebral artery spasms (vasospasm), leading to lack of oxygen in the distal supply territories, as well as the delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) constitute with 30% a high proportion of the complications. As a result, approximately 40-50% of patients suffer from permanent brain damage, which could lead to neurological deficits and intensive care over a long period of time. One promising treatment to prevent these complications is the medication with magnesium sulfate. Clinical trials showed that dosis, concentration in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) as well as timing of application are playing a major role in the application of magnesium sulfate.

Main purpose: 
The aim of this study is to measure the concentrations of magnesium and calcium in the cerebrospinal fluid during continuous application of magnesium sulfate in patients with aneurysmatic SAH. The results could lead to identify potential factors that have an impact on the treatment of secondary complications such as cerebral vasospasm or delayed cerebral ischemia.

Study Participants:
Patients with aneurysmatic SAH, treated within 24 hours after onset of bleeding either by microsurgical clipping or endovascular treatment, and receiving an external CSF drainage.

interventions.name:
At the beginning of surgery/endovascular treatment, all patients routinely receive i.v. nimodipin 1.0 mg/h over 6 hours, following 2.0 mg/h for 7 days dependent on the mean arterial blood pressure (>80 mm Hg). During the 7th and 14th day after SAH, nimodipin 6x60 mg/d is given orally.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
a) Minimum age of 18 years, both genders.
b) Written informed consent of the participant or his/her legal guardian
c) Patients with imaging-proof of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage 
d) Endovascular or microsurgical treatment within 12 hours after onset of SAH plus implantation of an external CSF drainage.
Exclusion criteria:
a) pregnancy and  breastfeeding
b) bodyweight <50kg
c) decompensated kidney disease (GFR <15ml/min)
d) acute coronary syndrome within the past 6 months
e) expected survival <48 hours
